messages.author: 8333ea3dc9d36457
messages.subject: How to control the distance between panels when using grid  (multi-panels figures)
parts:
Hi,
I constructed a multipanel figure using the little funciton in ggplot2
(example in the book).
However, my supervisor think the default distance between panels are
too wide.
Is there any way I could reduce the margin between panels to any value
I want? Thank you very much.

This is the funciton I uesed:

pdf("elFig2.pdf",width=6.84,height=6.84,paper="letter")
grid.newpage()
pushViewport(viewport(layout=grid.layout(3,3)))

# a little function.
vplayout<-function(x,y)
viewport(layout.pos.row=x,layout.pos.col=y)

print(mo2Hf2,vp=vplayout(1,1))
print(mo2St2,vp=vplayout(1,2))
print(mo2Fs2,vp=vplayout(1,3))
print(mo2Nf2,vp=vplayout(2,1))
print(mo2Bc2,vp=vplayout(2,2))
print(mo2Eco2,vp=vplayout(2,3))
print(mo2Ori2,vp=vplayout(3,1))
dev.off()

Anyone could point out the direction? Please. Million thanks.

John

question. Look at ?grid.layout and see if a vector of widths might help
you. ggplot2 loads grid automatically, but if you haven't loaded
ggplot2 then load grid.

messages.subject: Re: How to control the distance between panels when using grid  (multi-panels figures)
parts:
Hi,

You could set the plot margins of the individual plots. Compare the following,


plots = lapply(1:5, function(.x) qplot(1:10,rnorm(10),main=paste("plot",.x)))
source("http://gridextra.googlecode.com/svn/trunk/R/arrange.r")
do.call(arrange, plots)

plots2 = lapply(plots, function(.p) .p + opts(plot.margin =
unit(rep(0,4), "lines")))
dev.new()
do.call(arrange, plots2)


HTH,

baptiste

On Fri, Apr 16, 2010 at 9:23 PM, R is complicated <rinec...@gmail.com> wrote:
> lol. I see what you meant now. Thanks Baptiste.
>
> BTW, do you know how to show the default margin? Thank you.

the default values could depend on the theme, which you can access with

theme_grey()$plot.margin

You can visualize them graphically too (I never remember which way
around they go),

require(grid)

testMargins <- function(margins=unit(rep(1, 4), "lines")){
## the order is (bottom, left, top, right)
grid.newpage()
grid.rect(x=unit(c( 0.5, 0.1, 0.5, 0.9), "npc") -
unit.c( unit(0, "npc"), margins[2]*0.5, unit(0, "npc"),
-0.5*margins[4]),
y=unit(c(0.1, 0.5, 0.9, 0.5), "npc") -
unit.c(margins[1]*0.5, unit(0, "npc"), -0.5*margins[3],
unit(0, "npc")),
width=unit.c(unit(0.8, "npc"), margins[2], unit(0.8,
"npc"), margins[4]),
height=unit.c(margins[1], unit(0.8, "npc"), margins[3],
unit(0.8, "npc")))

grid.text(paste("margin", 1:4, "\n(", as.character(margins), ")"),
x=unit(c( 0.5, 0.1, 0.5, 0.9), "npc") -
unit.c( unit(0, "npc"), margins[2]*0.5, unit(0,
"npc"), -0.5*margins[4]),
y=unit(c(0.1, 0.5, 0.9, 0.5), "npc") -
unit.c(margins[1]*0.5, unit(0, "npc"),
-0.5*margins[3], unit(0, "npc")),
rot=c(0, 90, 0, 90))

}

testMargins(theme_grey()$plot.margin)


baptiste
